body:
## Goal
Evaluate upgrading FjordSide (internal repo: Pillagers) to Three.js r187 for alpha v0.1, with measurable performance, memory and rendering benefits. **Technical spike only: do not upgrade production by default.**

References:
- https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/releases/tag/r187
- https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/wiki/Migration-Guide

## Scope
### 1. Baseline and compatibility audit
- Record current Three.js version, renderer (WebGL/WebGPU), dependency constraints and build tooling.
- Inventory custom shaders/materials, water/sky/terrain/snow, aurora work, shadows/lighting, postprocessing, instancing/BatchedMesh, disposal and procedural island generation.
- Read the actual r187 release notes and migration guide; identify breaking changes and relevant improvements. Do not assume a feature applies to the renderer or code path in use.

### 2. Isolated upgrade experiment
- Create a separate branch; upgrade Three.js and required compatible dependencies only.
- Fix compilation/runtime regressions without broad refactors.
- Preserve WebGL compatibility, particularly iOS Safari. Treat WebGPU as a **separate optional feasibility experiment**, not a prerequisite.
- Compare screenshots for terrain blending, water, sky, snow, lighting, shadows, character materials and UI.

### 3. Reproducible A/B benchmarks
Use identical island seed, settings, device, viewport, graphics quality and simulation duration before/after. Record:
- Total load time and stage timings (world generation, geometry, textures, shader compilation, first render).
- FPS, p50/p95 frame times, main-thread stalls and draw calls/triangles.
- JS heap (where supported), GPU/renderer resource counters, memory growth after island regeneration/save-load, and disposal behavior.
- Desktop and iPhone Safari; report device/browser and thermal state.
- At least one sustained run with settlements, characters, wildlife and expeditions.

### 4. Findings and recommendation
- Publish a before/after comparison table, screenshots, regressions and clear attribution of any improvement.
- Distinguish engine improvements from changes in application code.
- Give a go/no-go recommendation for alpha v0.1; do not merge automatically.
- If bottlenecks are CPU simulation or procedural world generation rather than Three.js, document follow-up optimization opportunities instead of claiming the upgrade fixes them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Current version/renderer and affected code paths documented.
- [ ] r187 migration risks validated against official sources.
- [ ] Isolated branch builds and loads on desktop and iPhone Safari.
- [ ] Reproducible baseline vs r187 measurements with raw diagnostics.
- [ ] Visual regression checklist completed.
- [ ] No known resource leaks or new critical regressions.
- [ ] Explicit recommendation: adopt, defer or reject, with evidence.

**Out of scope:** Full WebGPU migration, redesign of terrain/water/aurora, unrelated optimization rewrites.
title: [Spike] Evaluate Three.js r187 upgrade for FjordSide alpha v0.1
